quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: The Strait of Juan de Fuca, which you can see from Port Angeles, was named after a Greek sailor who sailed for Spain under a Spanish name! His real name was Ioannis Phokas, but he became known as Juan de Fuca when he claimed to have discovered the passage in 1592.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Hummingbirds
short_read.teaser: These tiny jewels of the sky can fly backwards and their hearts beat up to 1,200 times per minute! Learn about the amazing adaptations that make hummingbirds such special visitors to Pacific Northwest gardens.

medium_read.title: Olympic National Park's Incredible Biodiversity
medium_read.teaser: From temperate rainforests to alpine meadows, the Olympic Peninsula contains ecosystems found nowhere else on Earth. Discover why this treasure in your backyard is one of the most ecologically diverse places in North America.

long_read.title: The Great Migration of Monarchs
long_read.teaser: Every year, millions of monarch butterflies travel up to 3,000 miles in one of nature's most remarkable journeys. This beautifully illustrated article follows their ancient migration route and the mystery of how they navigate.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer Season in Port Angeles
port_angeles.description: September is a wonderful time to spot black-tailed deer around Port Angeles, especially in the early morning or evening hours. These graceful animals are preparing for fall and are often seen near the edges of forests and meadows throughout the Olympic Peninsula.

puzzle_1.question: A ruby-throated hummingbird's wings beat about ___ times per second during normal flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right! That's about 3,180 beats per minute — so fast they create that lovely humming sound!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! The answer is 53 beats per second — that's about 3,180 times per minute!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 53 beats per second! That's so fast it creates the humming sound we hear when they fly by.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds can beat their wings even faster during courtship displays — up to 200 beats per second! This incredible speed requires tremendous energy, which is why they need to eat constantly.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is such a beautiful word for these delicate creatures!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'pillangó' — such a lovely, musical word! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The Hungarian word 'pillangó' is thought to come from an old word meaning 'to flutter' or 'to flicker,' perfectly describing how butterflies move through the air. Hungary is home to over 200 butterfly species!

puzzle_3.question: What do gardeners call the practice of planting flowers and herbs that attract beneficial insects like butterflies and bees?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Pollinator gardening helps support bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds — and makes for a beautiful, lively garden!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is pollinator gardening! It's a wonderful way to help butterflies, bees, and other beneficial insects while enjoying beautiful blooms. Companion planting is also beneficial, but it focuses on plants helping each other grow.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Native plants are especially valuable for pollinator gardens because local insects have evolved alongside them. In the Pacific Northwest, plants like Oregon grape, salal, and red flowering currant are excellent choices.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Pollinator gardening tips — National Park Service
